answer: Each identity registers one walnut crate stack at a tundra depot, locking a 70-credit bond. Its serial and weight enter a depot log under a key-bound cipher code only its owner can make. An auditor recomputes volume from the public crate table and scale log; a 2% mismatch, a missing crate, or a reused seal burns the bond. The first stack costs 32, the kth 32+6(k-1), the 1,000th 6,026, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,029,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-crate ring fails because a rented seal cannot validate a second stack. An honest depot pays 32 once and recovers its bond after audit.
